newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of Spain sees Q3 real GDP growth at two pct.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Spain sees Q3 real GDP growth at two pct.

text.p: The Bank of Spain forecast on Friday third-quarter gross domestic product had grown about two percent, little changed from 1.9 percent in quarter two.

"With the available data for this period, we estimate that year-on-year quarterly growth of real GDP will have been on the order of two percent, not very different from the past two quarters either in magnitude or in composition," the Bank of Spain said in its monthly report.
National demand could also have risen by two percent, slightly above 1.8 percent in the prior quarter. Private consumption was seen stagnant compared to the first half.

"Private consumption is not giving off signs of having become more dynamic than in the first half of the year, although by expressing growth in terms of year-on-year quarterly rise one could obtain a slightly higher real variation rate for the economy," the Bank of Spain said.
According to the Bank of Spain, economic data reveal that growth in Spain is running parallel to that of other European economies although at a slightly higher level than the average.

The report said Spain's economy possesses "a notable solidity and stability, not only for its composition but also because there are important corrections going on in the economy's basic imbalances - the rate of inflation is declining, balance of payments has been cleansed, and the process of fiscal consolidation is continuing," it said.
The Bank of Spain said it expected the economy to end the eyar and begin the enxt "with more elevated levels of real growth that can be maintained medium term."
